examples.ko: 난롯불 앞에 앉아서 얼어 있던 손을 녹였어요.
examples.en: I sat in front of the stove fire and warmed my frozen hands.

examples.ko: 밤새 난롯불이 꺼지지 않게 계속 지켜봤어요.
examples.en: I kept watching all night so the stove fire wouldn't go out.

examples.ko: 난롯불에 고구마를 구워 먹으면 정말 맛있어요.
examples.en: Sweet potatoes roasted over a stove fire taste really good.

examples.ko: 할머니는 난롯불을 쬐면서 옛날이야기를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother told me old stories while warming herself by the stove fire.
The stove fire is so warm that I'm getting sleepy.
The room was cold, so I lit the stove fire first.

explain: '난로'는 기계나 도구 자체이고, '난롯불'은 그 안에서 타는 불이에요. 장작이나 석탄 난로가 나오는 장면에서 자연스럽고, 'ㅅ'을 붙여 '난롯불'로 써요.
explain_en: '난로' is the heater itself, while '난롯불' is the fire burning inside it. It fits scenes with wood or coal stoves, and you write it with a 'ㅅ' as '난롯불'.

examples.ko: 한류와 난류가 만나는 바다에는 물고기가 많아요.
examples.en: Fish are plentiful in seas where cold and warm currents meet.

examples.ko: 난류가 흐르는 지역은 겨울에도 비교적 따뜻해요.
examples.en: Regions where a warm current flows are relatively warm even in winter.
A warm current passes near Jeju Island.

examples.ko: 난류를 따라 올라오는 물고기를 잡는 배가 많아요.
examples.en: Many boats catch the fish that swim up along the warm current.

examples.ko: 지구가 따뜻해지면서 난류의 영향이 커지고 있대요.
examples.en: I heard the influence of warm currents is growing as the Earth warms.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 난류와 한류의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned the difference between warm and cold currents in class.

explain: 반대말은 '한류'이고, 둘이 짝으로 자주 나와요. 일상 대화보다는 지리 수업, 날씨, 뉴스에서 만나는 말이에요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '한류' (cold current), and the two often appear as a pair. You meet it in geography class, weather reports and the news rather than in everyday talk.

en: proliferation; too many springing up without order

examples.ko: 후보 난립으로 표가 여러 갈래로 나뉘었어요.
examples.en: The flood of candidates split the votes many ways.

examples.ko: 난립이 심해서 어떤 가게가 좋은지 알기 어려워요.
examples.en: There are so many of them that it's hard to tell which shop is good.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 간판 난립 때문에 거리가 어지러워 보여요.
examples.en: This area looks messy because signs are crammed in everywhere.

examples.ko: 정부는 업체 난립을 막기 위해 기준을 강화했어요.
examples.en: The government tightened standards to stop companies from springing up everywhere.
The proliferation eventually led to chaos in the market.

examples.ko: 정당 난립에 대해 시민들의 불만이 커요.
examples.en: Citizens are increasingly unhappy about the glut of political parties.

explain: 보통 '후보 난립', '간판 난립'처럼 앞에 명사를 붙여서 써요. 질서 없이 너무 많이 생겼다는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is usually used after a noun, as in '후보 난립' or '간판 난립'. It carries a negative feeling that there are too many of something with no order.

en: proliferate; spring up everywhere without order

examples.en: During election season so many candidates run that it's hard to choose.
Shops are crammed into every alley in my neighborhood.
When too many similar apps pop up, users get confused.
A street crowded with signs looks messy.
They made rules so that cram schools wouldn't spring up everywhere.

examples.ko: 난립하는 업체 중에서 믿을 만한 곳을 찾기 힘들어요.
examples.en: Among the countless companies, it's hard to find a trustworthy one.

explain: 후보, 업체, 가게, 간판처럼 여럿이 질서 없이 마구 생길 때 써요. 좋은 일에는 쓰지 않고 '너무 많아서 문제'라는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Use it when candidates, companies, shops or signs appear in large numbers without order. It is not used for good things; it implies there are too many and that's a problem.

examples.en: They say heroes appear in troubled times.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공은 난세를 살아가는 평범한 사람이에요.
examples.en: The main character in the movie is an ordinary person living through turbulent times.
The more troubled the times, the more you feel how precious family is.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 난세의 백성들 이야기를 다뤄요.
examples.en: This novel deals with the stories of common people in turbulent times.

examples.ko: 난세에 태어난 사람들은 힘든 삶을 살았어요.
examples.en: People born in troubled times lived hard lives.

examples.ko: 사람들은 요즘 같은 때를 난세라고 말하기도 해요.
examples.en: Some people call times like these turbulent times.

explain: 전쟁이나 혼란으로 어지러운 시대를 말하고, 반대로 평화로운 때는 '태평성대'라고 해요. 역사, 사극, 소설에 많이 나오고 '난세에 영웅 난다'라는 말로도 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It refers to an era disordered by war or chaos; a peaceful era is '태평성대'. It appears often in history, historical dramas and novels, and in the saying '난세에 영웅 난다' (heroes arise in troubled times).

examples.en: That story is complete nonsense.
Let me give you a fun nonsense quiz.
I think a rule like this is nonsense.

examples.ko: 친구가 낸 난센스 문제에 다 같이 웃었어요.
examples.en: We all laughed at the riddle my friend posed.

examples.ko: 어른들도 난센스 같은 일에 휘둘릴 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Even adults sometimes get pushed around by absurd things.
Nonsense comedies are funny because the plots are so wacky.

explain: '말도 안 되는 일'이라고 비판할 때도 쓰고, 엉뚱한 말장난을 하는 '난센스 퀴즈'로도 많이 써요. '넌센스'가 아니라 '난센스'로 써요.
explain_en: It can criticize something as absurd, and it is also used for silly wordplay riddles called '난센스 퀴즈'. The standard spelling is '난센스', not '넌센스'.

examples.ko: 이 계획에는 몇 가지 난점이 있어요.
examples.en: This plan has a few difficulties.

examples.ko: 가장 큰 난점은 시간이 부족하다는 거예요.
examples.en: The biggest difficulty is that we don't have enough time.

examples.ko: 난점을 먼저 정리해야 해결 방법이 보여요.
examples.en: You have to sort out the difficulties first to see a solution.

examples.ko: 이 방법의 난점에 대해 의견을 나눴어요.
examples.en: We exchanged opinions about the difficulties of this method.
What is counted as the main difficulty is the cost.
There are many difficulties, but the advantages are clear too.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '어려운 점'이라고 많이 말하고, '난점'은 발표나 보고서 같은 글에서 써요. '문제점'은 잘못된 부분이고, '난점'은 해결하기 까다로운 부분이라는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: In everyday talk people often say '어려운 점', while '난점' fits presentations and reports. '문제점' is a faulty part, whereas '난점' is a part that is tricky to solve.

examples.ko: 요즘 우리 팀의 경기력이 난조를 보이고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team's performance has been in a slump lately.
The pitcher fell into a slump from the early innings.

examples.ko: 컨디션 난조로 오늘 경기에 못 나왔어요.
examples.en: He couldn't play today because he was off form.
As the slump dragged on, the coach replaced the player.
I move carefully when the market is unstable.
I practice every day to get out of my slump.

explain: '난조를 보이다', '난조에 빠지다'처럼 컨디션, 실력, 경기, 시장이 평소처럼 안정되지 않을 때 써요. 스포츠 중계나 뉴스에서 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '컨디션이 안 좋다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is used in patterns like '난조를 보이다' and '난조에 빠지다' when condition, skill, a game or a market is not stable as usual. It is common in sports commentary and news, while in daily talk people say '컨디션이 안 좋다'.

examples.ko: 폭풍 때문에 배가 난파 위기에 처했어요.
examples.en: The ship was in danger of being wrecked because of the storm.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 난파 사고에서 살아남은 사람들 이야기예요.
examples.en: This movie is about people who survived a shipwreck.
The rescue team searched for survivors at the wreck site.
The captain changed course to avoid being wrecked.

examples.ko: 오래전 난파로 바다 밑에 가라앉은 보물이 있대요.
examples.en: They say there is treasure that sank to the seabed in an old shipwreck.
The cause of the shipwreck was the fierce waves.

explain: 배가 부서지거나 가라앉는 일에 써요. 항공기 사고에는 보통 '추락'이라고 하고, 난파는 사고 뉴스나 모험 이야기에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It refers to a ship breaking up or sinking. For airplane accidents people usually say '추락' instead, and '난파' appears in accident news and adventure stories.

examples.en: An old shipwreck was found at the bottom of the sea.
Divers are examining the wreck.
Lots of old ceramics were recovered from the wreck.
In the movie, the main character gets trapped in a wrecked ship.
Debris from the wreck washed up onto the beach.

examples.ko: 그 낡은 배는 마치 난파선 같아요.
examples.en: That old boat looks just like a shipwreck.

explain: 부서지거나 가라앉은 배 자체를 말해요. 낡고 망가진 배를 보고 '난파선 같다'고 비유해서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the broken or sunken ship itself. People also use it figuratively, saying an old, battered boat is 'like a wreck' ('난파선 같다').

en: being almost equal; having trouble telling which is better

examples.ko: 두 후보 실력이 난형난제라서 결과를 예측하기 어려워요.
examples.en: The two candidates are so evenly matched that the result is hard to predict.

examples.ko: 둘 다 요리를 잘해서 정말 난형난제예요.
examples.en: They both cook so well that it's hard to say who's better.

examples.ko: 형제의 키가 난형난제여서 누가 더 큰지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: The brothers are so close in height that I can't tell who is taller.
This final was a contest between two evenly matched sides.
The two teams are going head to head, neck and neck.

examples.ko: 난형난제인 두 선수를 보며 관중이 숨을 죽였어요.
examples.en: The crowd held its breath watching the two evenly matched players.

explain: 둘 다 비슷하게 뛰어나서 누가 더 나은지 가리기 어려울 때 써요. 보통 '난형난제이다'처럼 서술어로 쓰고, '막상막하'도 비슷한 상황에서 써요.
explain_en: Use it when two are both so good that it's hard to say which is better. It is usually used as a predicate ('난형난제이다'), and '막상막하' fits a similar situation.

examples.en: The rice ripened and the grains turned yellow.
Sparrows pick up and eat grains in the paddy.
Grandfather begrudged even a single fallen grain.
The grains ripened firmly in the sunshine.

examples.ko: 밥을 먹을 때 낟알 하나까지 남기지 않으려고 해요.
examples.en: When I eat, I try not to leave even a single grain.
I picked out only the grains and put them in a sack.

explain: 곡식의 알 하나하나를 말해요. '이삭'은 알이 달린 줄기 부분이고, '낟알'은 거기서 나온 알이에요. 소리 나는 대로 [나달], '낟알이'는 [나다리]로 읽어요.
explain_en: It means the individual kernels of grain. '이삭' is the ear of the plant where grains grow, and '낟알' is the grains themselves. It is read [나달], and '낟알이' is read [나다리].

examples.en: This price is downright robbery.
Overcharging like that, he's nothing but a highway robber.

examples.ko: 그 가게 주인은 손님한테 날강도처럼 굴었어요.
examples.en: The shop owner acted like a robber toward customers.

examples.ko: 수리비를 열 배나 받다니 날강도 아니에요?
examples.en: Charging ten times as much for repairs, isn't that robbery?
People call that company a bunch of robbers.
I feel like I was robbed blind.

explain: 진짜 강도보다는 터무니없이 비싼 값을 받거나 뻔뻔하게 빼앗는 사람이나 가게를 욕할 때 많이 써요. 거친 말이라 공식적인 자리나 윗사람 앞에서는 피해요.
explain_en: It is more often used to scold people or shops that charge outrageous prices or take things shamelessly than for actual robbers. It is a harsh word, so avoid it in formal settings or around elders.

examples.en: Our cat is really quick.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 몸이 날래서 상대가 잡지 못해요.
examples.en: That player is so nimble that opponents can't catch him.
He caught the ball with a swift move.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 다람쥐처럼 날래게 나무를 탔어요.
examples.en: The child climbed the tree swiftly like a squirrel.
If your hands are quick, cooking finishes fast too.

examples.ko: 날래지 못한 저는 항상 늦게 도착해요.
examples.en: I'm not quick, so I always arrive late.

explain: '빠르다'가 속도 전반을 말한다면 '날래다'는 몸이나 손의 움직임이 재빠르다는 느낌이에요. 대화에서는 '빠르다', '재빠르다'를 쓰기도 하고, 불규칙 없이 '날래요', '날랜'으로 활용해요.
explain_en: While '빠르다' covers speed in general, '날래다' feels like quick movement of the body or hands. In conversation people may also say '빠르다' or '재빠르다', and it conjugates regularly: '날래요', '날랜'.

examples.en: The cat leapt nimbly onto the wall.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 날렵히 날아온 공을 피했어요.
examples.en: The player nimbly dodged the incoming ball.
He slipped nimbly through the gap in the door.
The squirrel climbs up the tree nimbly.

examples.ko: 점원이 날렵히 손님 짐을 들어 줬어요.
examples.en: The clerk deftly lifted the customer's bags.
I turned my body nimbly and didn't bump into anything.

explain: 몸놀림이 가볍고 재빠를 때 써요. 형용사 '날렵하다'는 몸매나 차의 모양에도 쓰지만, 부사 '날렵히'는 주로 동작을 꾸며요. '날렵하게'로 말해도 돼요.
explain_en: Use it when movement is light and quick. The adjective '날렵하다' can also describe a slim build or a car's shape, but the adverb '날렵히' mostly describes actions. You can also say '날렵하게'.

examples.en: The child snatched up a cookie and gobbled it down.

examples.ko: 강아지가 내 손에 있던 간식을 날름 가져갔어요.
examples.en: The puppy swiped the snack right out of my hand.

examples.ko: 동생이 내 몫까지 날름 먹어 버렸어요.
examples.en: My little brother quickly ate my share too.
The snake flicked out its tongue.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 선물을 날름 받더니 인사도 안 했어요.
examples.en: He grabbed the gift and didn't even say thanks.
My friend quickly took my seat.

explain: 혀를 재빨리 내밀거나 무언가를 재빨리 집어 먹거나 가져가는 모양이에요. 약간 얄밉거나 귀여운 느낌이 있고, '날름날름'처럼 반복해서도 써요.
explain_en: It describes a tongue flicking out or something being snatched or eaten in a flash. It has a slightly cheeky or cute feel, and can be repeated as '날름날름'.

en: dart one's tongue in and out

examples.en: That snake over there keeps flicking its tongue.

examples.ko: 강아지가 물을 마실 때 혀를 날름거리면서 마셔요.
examples.en: The puppy laps up water, flicking its tongue.
It was fascinating to watch the lizard flick its tongue.
Flames flickered inside the stove.
Don't flick your tongue around; eat politely.
The child flicked out his tongue at the sight of the ice cream.

explain: 혀나 불길이 자꾸 빠르게 나왔다 들어갔다 하는 모습에 써요. '날름대다'와 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: Use it when a tongue or flame keeps darting in and out quickly. It can be swapped with '날름대다' with the same meaning.

en: dart one's tongue in and out

examples.en: The cat flicks its tongue while drinking milk.
The frog flicked its tongue to catch a fly.
I sat in front of the stove where the flames flickered.

examples.ko: 혀를 날름대지 마세요, 보기 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Please don't flick your tongue; it doesn't look nice.
The baby flicks its tongue while waiting for its baby food.
When a snake flicks its tongue, I get scared for no reason.

explain: '날름거리다'와 같은 뜻이고, '-거리다'와 '-대다'는 서로 바꿔 써도 돼요. 혀나 불길이 빠르게 움직일 때 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '날름거리다', and '-거리다' and '-대다' are interchangeable here. Use it when a tongue or flame moves quickly.

examples.ko: 이 집은 날림으로 지어서 비가 새요.
examples.en: This house was built sloppily, so the roof leaks.

examples.ko: 날림 공사는 나중에 큰 문제가 돼요.
examples.en: Slipshod construction becomes a big problem later.

examples.ko: 날림이라서 며칠 못 가서 고장 났어요.
examples.en: It was shoddily made, so it broke within a few days.
That report is completely slapdash.

examples.ko: 날림 제품은 싸지만 오래 못 써요.
examples.en: Shoddy products are cheap but don't last long.

examples.ko: 날림으로 일하면 결국 다시 해야 해요.
examples.en: If you work sloppily, you end up having to redo it.

explain: 공사나 물건, 일을 서둘러 대충 한 것을 말하고 부정적인 느낌이에요. '날림 공사', '날림으로'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많고, 비슷한 말로 '부실', '대충'이 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to work, goods or construction done in a rush and carelessly, with a negative feel. It often appears as '날림 공사' or '날림으로', and similar words are '부실' and '대충'.

examples.ko: 며칠 날밤을 새워서 오늘에야 작품을 끝냈어요.
examples.en: After staying up several nights, I finally finished the work today.

examples.ko: 날밤은 새웠지만 숙제는 아직 못 끝냈어요.
examples.en: I pulled an all-nighter, but I still haven't finished my homework.

examples.ko: 친구와 게임하다가 날밤을 새운 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once stayed up all night playing games with a friend.
Staying up all night is not good for your health.
The baby was sick, so the parents stayed up all night.
I prepared this presentation even staying up all night, so I'm nervous.

explain: 거의 '날밤을 새우다'라는 표현으로만 써요. '밤을 새우다'와 비슷하지만 '날밤'은 한숨도 못 자고 지새운 밤이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is used almost only in the expression '날밤을 새우다'. It is similar to '밤을 새우다', but '날밤' feels more like a night without any sleep at all.

en: sudden thunderbolt; bolt from the blue

examples.ko: 갑자기 회사가 문을 닫는다니 이게 무슨 날벼락이에요?
examples.en: The company is suddenly closing? What a bolt from the blue!

examples.ko: 선생님이 꼼꼼하셔서 숙제를 안 내면 날벼락이 떨어져요.
examples.en: My teacher is meticulous, so if you skip homework you get a real scolding.

examples.ko: 시험 전날 갑자기 날벼락 같은 소식을 들었어요.
examples.en: The day before the exam I suddenly heard shocking news.
Walking down the street, I felt as if I had been struck by lightning.
The layoff notice hit our family like a bolt from the blue.

examples.ko: 엄마의 날벼락 같은 목소리에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by my mom's thunderous voice.

explain: 원래는 맑은 날 갑자기 치는 벼락이지만, 지금은 예상 못 한 나쁜 일이나 갑작스러운 큰 꾸중을 말할 때 더 많이 써요. '날벼락이 떨어지다', '날벼락을 맞다'로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: Out of nowhere, the exam was suddenly canceled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전혀 예상하지 못한 일이 갑자기 일어났을 때 써요. 주로 나쁜 일에 쓰지만 놀란 감정을 강조하기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something completely unexpected happens suddenly, mostly bad news, to stress the shock.

explain_en: Originally it is lightning striking suddenly on a clear day, but now it is often used for an unexpected bad event or a sudden harsh scolding. It commonly appears as '날벼락이 떨어지다' or '날벼락을 맞다'.

examples.ko: 숨을 깊이 들이마시고 날숨을 천천히 내쉬세요.
examples.en: Breathe in deeply and slowly breathe out.
In yoga, you relax your body on the exhale.
When your exhale gets longer, your mind relaxes.

examples.ko: 달리기할 때는 들숨과 날숨의 리듬이 중요해요.
examples.en: When running, the rhythm of inhaling and exhaling is important.

examples.ko: 날숨은 입보다 코로 쉬는 게 편해요.
examples.en: It's more comfortable to exhale through the nose than the mouth.

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 날숨마다 하얀 입김이 나왔어요.
examples.en: On the cold day, white breath came out with every exhale.

explain: 반대말은 '들숨'이고, 둘을 함께 '호흡'이라고 해요. 보통 '날숨을 내쉬다'처럼 말하고, 운동, 요가, 건강 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '들숨' (inhale). People usually say '날숨을 내쉬다', and it often comes up in talk about exercise, yoga and health.
